D.t: Doug Jones trails by 11.1 and wins 4% of simulations. Closing it takes about 95,077 voters switching sides, or 190,155 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +18.7 and R +3.2. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The polls page average is R +11.1. Your best recent poll is Cygnal (R) for Gray Media and Alabama Daily News at R +10.1; your worst is Napolitan News Service/RMG Research for Alabama Policy Action (R) at R +11.2. 2 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Jefferson, a projected net 88,841 votes; Montgomery, a projected net 30,565 votes; Madison, a projected net 20,754 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Mobile, D +9.2, 7.7% of the vote; Tuscaloosa, D +5.5, 3.9% of the vote; Lee, R +9.7, 3.1% of the vote; Talladega, R +11.6, 1.5% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Doug Jones runs furthest behind in Cullman, DeKalb, Marshall. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters without a degree, 69% of voters, 40 to 59, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.43 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 63% of voters, 44 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.14 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 59% of voters, 47 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.96 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Doug Jones: Immigration voters 18 to 81, White voters 34 to 65, Small counties 35 to 64. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.2M cash against $6.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points away from Doug Jones. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Cash: $6.5M in the bank against $2.2M for Doug Jones.
